sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic, French-inspired code law system)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (Companies Act of 1915), Articles 944-1 et seq. (SCSp regime introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013); Loi modifiée du 19 décembre 2002 concernant le registre de commerce et des sociétés (RCS Law), Articles 1 and 9; Loi du 13 janvier 2019 sur le registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE Law).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Constitutional deed (acte de constitution — partnership agreement / contrat de société) in notarial or private-writing form, filed electronically via the LBR e-filing portal (Form E-01 'Demande d'inscription').
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital is required for an SCSp; the capital amount, contribution terms and payment schedule are freely set in the partnership agreement; no escrow account or bank attestation of deposit is mandated by Luxembourg company law. The limited partner's obligation to contribute becomes binding upon execution of the constitutional deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the Limited Partnership Agreement of the SCSp, signed by all founding partners, is hereby ratified and adopted as the governing charter of the Special Limited Partnership.
RESOLVED, that the initial cash subscription of the Sole Limited Partner for [number] Partnership Interests is accepted and subscribed; no statutory minimum capital or escrow deposit applies under Luxembourg law.
RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [Address], Luxembourg.
RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Managing Partner and day-to-day Gérant with full powers to open bank accounts, engage service providers, and file with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) and the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA.
RESOLVED FURTHER, that all prior acts consistent with these resolutions are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitutional Deed Appraisal, Execution and Legalization of the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (if notarial form elected) or the founding partners by private deed (acte sous seing privé); advised by a member of the Luxembourg Bar.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and approve the partnership agreement identifying at least one general partner (commandité, unlimited liability) and one limited partner (commanditaire). If the general partner is a corporate vehicle, obtain its articles, RCS extract and board resolution. Execute the deed by all partners; notarize if real property is contributed or if investors require a certified deed, then attend to sworn translations and legalization of foreign signatures.
required_dossiers: Signed SCSp partnership agreement (acte sous seing privé or notarial deed)
Articles of association and RCS extract of the corporate general partner (if any)
Board resolution of the corporate general partner authorizing the SCSp formation
Valid passports/IDs of all partners and of the appointed Gérant
Criminal record (extrait du casier judiciaire) or sworn declaration of non-bankruptcy of the Gérant
Proof of registered-office address (lease or domiciliation agreement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or a partner's counsel flags formal defects (defective powers of attorney, incorrect identity or address details), the parties execute a rectification rider (avenant) and, where required, re-notarize before any RCS filing is made; the cure typically completes within 2-3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Bank Account and Effectuation of Initial Capital Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution subject to CSSF supervision (Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Gérant opens a corporate account in the name of the SCSp (the account mandate being executed by the corporate general partner). Deposit the agreed cash contribution and/or pledge in-kind contributions as provided in the partnership agreement. No statutory escrow deposit exists; the bank will apply standard KYC/AML due diligence on the partners and beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement (banker's copy)
KYC/AML questionnaire and account mandate forms
Passports/IDs of partners and ultimate beneficial owners
Source-of-funds/source-of-wealth statement of the limited partner
RCS application copy evidencing the pending incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a documentary pending list, supply the requested UBO chart and source-of-funds evidence within 5 business days; if the account is refused, engage an alternate Luxembourg bank and complete the RCS filing within the statutory one-month period from execution of the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Registration Filing with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS Department, e-filing portal (guichet unique).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of execution of the constitutional deed, submit the online application Form E-01 together with the signed deed and the Gérant's declaration under Article 9 of the RCS Law. The RCS verifies the general partner's capacity and the legal conformity of the SCSp; upon approval it allocates the company registration number.
required_dossiers: RCS electronic application form (Formulaire E-01)
Certified copy of the constitutional deed
Declaration under Article 9 of the RCS Law (capacity/non-conviction)
Proof of payment of the state filing fee (EUR 49)
Where the general partner is a company: its RCS extract and powers of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On receipt of a query (demande de régularisation), the Gérant supplies the missing annexes through the LBR portal within the stated deadline (typically 30 days). If the filing misses the one-month deadline from signature, a corrective deed/resolution must be executed before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Publication in the RESA and Issuance of the RCS Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA); Ministry of Justice.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following registration, the RCS publishes the deed excerpt in the RESA, making the SCSp effective as against third parties, and issues the official RCS extract (extrait du RCS) confirming legal existence, registration number, registered office and the Gérant's mandate; the SCSp also becomes LEI-eligible.
required_dossiers: None (automatic statutory publication); the RCS issues the extract without additional filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If reservation or publication is delayed, the Gérant emails the RCS registration desk requesting expedited treatment; any material error in the published extract is corrected by a rectification application with the RCS, republished within 3-5 business days at no separate state fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, Beneficial Ownership and Social Security / Labour Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); LBR RBE register; Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp for VAT (if taxable turnover is projected), obtain the national business number (matricule), file the beneficial-ownership declaration with the RBE register within one month of RCS registration, register as an employer with the CCSS if staff are appointed, and file the workplace opening declaration with the ITM for the subscription-box warehouse/office.
required_dossiers: RCS extract (certificate of incorporation)
VAT and business-number registration forms (via AEDT / MyGuichet)
RBE beneficial-ownership declaration (e-form)
Lease or domiciliation agreement of the registered office
CCSS employer registration and ITM workplace declaration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late RBE/VAT filings carry administrative fines (up to EUR 50 per day up to statutory caps); submit the missing declarations with a reasoned mitigation plea to the AEDT or the RBE register and attach the RCS extract; penalties are contestable in writing within one month of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Agency) and the municipal building inspectorate of the commune where the fulfillment warehouse is located.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commune building/occupancy permit (autorisation de bâtir et d'exploitation) and, where the warehouse exceeds classification thresholds, an environmental operating permit under the Loi modifiée du 19 mars 2017 relative aux établissements classés; the permit is issued to the operating entity (the corporate general partner or a dedicated Luxembourg operating company).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement — Environmental Protection Agency, Luxembourg.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration/notification tier (Annex II-type): a full EIA under the Law of 15 May 2018 is not triggered for a subscription-box fulfillment warehouse below 10,000 m² storage and 2 ha site; communal nuisance screening (noise, traffic, waste) applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic wastewater to public sewer per the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 14 November 2014 (typical municipal limits: BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, TSS ≤ 35 mg/L); VOC emissions negligible for non-industrial packaging activity (EU Directive 2010/75/EU thresholds not reached); packaging and waste handling per the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management with proof of licensed waste streams.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification (attestation de sécurité incendie) from the Administration des services de secours (CGDIS) for the warehouse and office; structural-load certificate from the municipal building authority; electrical-installation conformity certificate; workplace clearance with the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM), appointment of a safety delegate, and annual occupational-safety update where staff exceeds regulatory thresholds.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and duties; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for income taxes; Administration des douanes et accises (ADA) for customs. Principal portals: MyGuichet.lu (business registry filings), eCDF (electronic VAT/customs filing), and the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) for company registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an SCSp: (1) Execute the partnership agreement (contrat de société; notarial deed required only if real estate is contributed) and file constitutive documents with the RCS through MyGuichet.lu; (2) obtain the national business number (OUID) from the RCS, which is the master company identifier; (3) complete VAT registration with the AEDT via the eCDF/MyGuichet.lu portal; the AEDT issues a separate VAT identification number in the format LU + 8 digits; (4) a non-resident foreign entity that has no Luxembourg establishment but is liable for Luxembourg VAT must register directly with the AEDT and appoint a local fiscal representative (représentant responsable de la TVA) approved by the AEDT; (5) where goods are imported or exported, the entity must hold an EORI number (LU + OUID) issued by the ADA. Total processing time: approximately 2 to 6 weeks from RCS filing to operative VAT number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the SCSp is a partnership without legal personality and is fiscally transparent for direct tax purposes: no corporate income tax, no municipal business tax, and no net wealth tax at entity level. Each partner is taxed on its allocable share of SCSp income under Luxembourg domestic law (corporate income tax for corporate partners; personal income tax for individual partners). A foreign partner is taxable in Luxembourg only on Luxembourg-source profits attributable to the SCSp. For VAT purposes, however, the SCSp is a separate taxable person with its own VAT registration. The SCSp does not qualify for the sheltered SPF (Société de Participations Financières) regime, which is limited to non-commercial holding vehicles.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists for the SCSp; fiscal transparency is mandatory under Luxembourg tax law as confirmed by Circular L.I.R. n° 14/4. Available elections include: (a) solidarity VAT grouping under article 60 of the Loi TVA, allowing the SCSp to be combined with its partners or certain related Luxembourg entities as a single taxable person for VAT; (b) the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) election for intra-EU distance sales of subscription boxes and the Import-One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) election for low-value consignments; (c) the small-business franchise exemption under article 57 of the Loi TVA, available only to Luxembourg-established taxable persons with annual turnover below EUR 35,000 (non-resident suppliers cannot apply); (d) ATAD-based hybrid-mismatch adjustments under the law of 21 December 2019, which may reclassify the SCSp as opaque where a foreign partner treats it as taxable for its own tax purposes; the SCSp must retain contemporaneous documentation of each partner's classification to avoid adverse recharacterization.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), governed by the Loi TVA of 12 February 1979 as amended, transposing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC. Reduced rates: 3% (super-reduced), 8% (reduced), 14% (intermediate for hospitality and certain services); standard rate 17%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for non-resident or non-established suppliers — VAT registration is mandatory from the first euro of taxable activity in Luxembourg. Luxembourg-established small businesses may apply the article 57 franchise exemption up to EUR 35,000 annual turnover. For intra-EU distance sales of goods to consumers (B2C), the annual EU-wide threshold is EUR 10,000; once exceeded, the destination member state's VAT must be collected through the OSS. B2B intra-EU acquisitions require a VAT number regardless of value.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping mandate applies in Luxembourg. Electronic invoicing is mandatory only for B2G transactions (to public entities via the PEPPOL network in PEPPOL BIS 3.0 format). Luxembourg has adopted legislation enabling mandatory B2B e-invoicing, expected to be phased in from 2026/2027 in line with the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package; however, no binding B2B e-invoice or API clearance requirement is currently in force. Invoices must satisfy the authenticity requirements of the Loi TVA (reliable audit trail, XML/EDI archive with readable representation), and invoices for exports or intra-EU supplies must include the required reference to the VAT exemption clause.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Subscription boxes physically dispatched to destinations outside the EU qualify for the 0% export rate under article 40 of the Loi TVA, provided the goods leave the EU within the administrative expectation of 90 days from dispatch and the export proof is retained. Intra-EU dispatches to taxable persons (B2B) are exempt as intra-Community supplies under article 39 of the Loi TVA if the recipient's valid EU VAT number is quoted on the invoice and in the recapitulative statement (EC Sales List). Intra-EU B2C distance sales are not zero-rated; they are taxable in the consumer's member state via the OSS (or at the Luxembourg rate if the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold is not exceeded). Subscription boxes containing excise goods, e.g., alcohol, tobacco, or mineral oil samples, are excluded from OSS, distance-sale simplifications, and standard zero-rating unless specific excise and customs conditions are satisfied. Ancillary international freight and logistics services related to the export of the boxes may be zero-rated under articles 42-43 of the Loi TVA.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / Document Unique d'Accompagnement) filed electronically with the Administration des douanes et accises (e-Customs/ECS), referencing the EORI/OUID number, HS codes, weights, and proof of exit from the European Union

Bill of Lading (sea), Air Waybill (air), or CMR consignment note (road) evidencing physical transport to a destination outside the EU; where the buyer arranges carriage, the seller must obtain a certificate of arrival or equivalent customs export proof within 90 days

Inward Remittance Certificate — bank statement, SWIFT MT103/MT202, or payment confirmation showing settlement by the foreign buyer. Luxembourg does not impose a statutory FX repatriation deadline, but a 180-day documented settlement window is recommended to substantiate commercial genuineness and to reduce AEDT audit challenge
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT audits of zero-rating claims focus on the completeness of the export evidence package (SAD, transport document, payment proof, and separate HS-code declaration). If zero-rating is disallowed, the AEDT retroactively assesses VAT at 17% on the supply price, plus default interest at 0.8% per month (9.6% per annum). Fraudulent claims — including falsely dated customs declarations, circular shipments, or misdescribed destinations — are prosecuted under article 65 of the Loi TVA, carrying fines from EUR 500 up to EUR 12,500 per violation (or one to five times the tax evaded in aggravated cases), publication of the sanction, and imprisonment of up to 5 years when referred to the criminal courts. The limitation period is 5 years for good-faith underdeclarations and 10 years in cases of fraud or bad faith. Where a rejected intra-EU B2B exemption results from an invalid or inactive recipient VAT number, the SCSp may be held jointly and severally liable for the counterparty's VAT under article 52 of the Loi TVA. Unsubstantiated export refunds are clawed back with interest and may trigger automatic audit of all subsequent zero-rating claims for the same product category.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) — Eurosystem member; monetary and FX policy set by the European Central Bank (ECB); banking supervision coordinated by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under the Luxembourg Law of 5 April 1993.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. Luxembourg maintains no exchange controls and imposes no prior authorisation requirement on current-account or capital-account flows, consistent with Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). Profit remittances and capital distributions from the SCSp are freely executable through authorised credit institutions; the only constraints are EU/UN financial sanctions (e.g., Council Regulation (EU) No 833/2014) and Luxembourg AML/CFT rules (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended). Cross-border payments require BCL balance-of-payments statistical purpose codes but do not require convertibility licences.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg does not impose surrender, repatriation deadlines, or conversion ratios on export proceeds. A subscription box exporter (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 454110) must only file statistical declarations to BCL/STATEC for balance-of-payments purposes and comply with VAT rules (reverse charge for B2B supplies of goods outside Luxembourg). All foreign currency may be retained freely in operational or escrow accounts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility. Luxembourg recognises CSSF-licensed payment institutions and e-money institutions under PSD2 (Law of 10 November 2009, amended) and the E-Money Law of 2 August 2011. EMIs issuing local IBANs (e.g., Satchel, Mangopay, Paydo, or passported EU EMIs registered with the CSSF through the EBA passporting framework) can lawfully serve the SCSp's cross-border subscription payments and hold safeguarded client funds. Legal constraints: (i) EMIs cannot provide credit to the SCSp; (ii) client funds must be safeguarded with a Tier-1 credit institution and are not covered by the Luxembourg deposit guarantee scheme (FGDL); (iii) the SCSp should maintain a separate Tier-1 bank account for capital escrow, FX collateral, and commercial LC issuances; (iv) card schemes (Stripe Billing, Authorize.Net) require an acquiring relationship — for the EU/EEA market, Stripe's Luxembourg/IE acquiring is acceptable, whereas Authorize.Net's legacy Visa Europe arrangement has limited EU-wide applicability and a local acquiring sponsor is recommended.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permissible under the Luxembourg Law of 25 March 2020 on electronic and virtual identification (as amended), provided eIDAS-certified identity verification and qualified electronic signatures are used. In practice, Tier-1 banks (BCEE, BIL, ING) require at least one physical or virtual interview with the General Partner's management board and visible UBOs; for a commercial SCSp with a low-risk subscription business, virtual KYC via the bank's approved video tool is acceptable without a Luxembourg notary if the General Partner provides a certified RCS excerpt, the RBE confirmation, and a notarially certified signature specimen. The SCSp, having legal personality, must be represented by its General Partner; each natural-person UBO holding more than 25% of the partnership must complete individual KYC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain opacity: the subscriber or contributing partner is an offshore corporate or another partnership with nominee shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extract from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); certified UBO declaration under Law of 13 January 2019; complete organisational chart with notifications of ownership through any intermediate holding entity; signed negative-confirmation letter from the General Partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: First capital injection exceeds EUR 50,000 without documentary source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital call / subscription agreement; banking statements of the contributing partner showing source account; source-of-wealth statement (sale agreement, loan agreement, dividends, or audited reserves); tax residence certificate; CSSF-standard declaration (no PEP/MI status).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP screening hit on the GP, partners, or trade counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU consolidated financial sanctions screening report (Regulations (EU) Nos 269/2014, 765/2006, 833/2014); OFAC non-US person analysis; PEP identification and risk-mitigation memo; sworn declarations and adverse-media check from a licensed compliance database.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance to support a recurring subscription business from Luxembourg
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance file under the Law of 17 December 2021: registered office lease, local manager / director appointment, Luxembourg bank mandate, annual subscription and transaction budget, supplier and customer contracts, marketing and customer-care minutes, and pro-forma VAT filings demonstrating real local management.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border card-based recurring revenue flagged for high-risk geography or excessive chargeback patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant-of-record agreement and processor (Stripe) settlement reports; EU transfer-of-funds information under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113; geo-blocking statement; PCI-DSS Level 1 certificate; GDPR Article 28 data processing agreements; chargeback and 3-D Secure (SCA) statistics for the prior 12 months.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions are routed by SWIFT MT103 (EEA: TARGET2/SEPA-equivalent) to the SCSp's EUR account at a Luxembourg bank. The remitter must encode BCL balance-of-payments purpose code 'F6' (direct investment, equity capital) or 'LF 8' (intercompany loan) and reference the SCSp's RCS number and the capital call identifier. The beneficiary bank verifies the partnership agreement, the GP resolution, the capital call notice, the UBO record, and applicable sanctions lists before crediting. Non-EUR injections are converted on the spot market without BCL approval. Chargebacks and returns are reconciled under the cash application schedule recorded in the subscription-box general ledger.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Three clearing rails: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant for EU suppliers settle via TARGET2; (ii) SWIFT MT103 / MT202 COV for non-EEA suppliers using gpi tracking and ISO 20022 purpose codes; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) in SWIFT MT700 format issued by the Luxembourg bank for merchandise imports. Customer subscription receipts are captured by the acquiring processor (Stripe Billing / European acquirer) and settled as EUR T+1 credits into the operating account; chargeback reserves and FX margin calls are cleared from a dedicated collateral account to decouple Treasury cash from customer receivables.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD and EUR/GBP delivered outright FX forwards
EUR/USD and EUR/GBP FX swaps (tom-next and longer-tenor rollovers)
European-style FX options and zero-premium collars
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) referencing €STR, SOFR and SONIA
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) solely for soft-currency third-country exposures, subject to EMIR uncleared margin rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 31 March; within one month after any ownership or control change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines from EUR 125 to EUR 1,250 per day of continued non-compliance; criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment for deliberate omissions; no automatic administrative strike-off solely for RBE non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) with the trade and companies register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date; for a 31 December year-end, due by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Judicial civil penalty (astreinte) of up to EUR 10,000 imposed by the District Court at the request of the Public Prosecutor; persistent non-filing may lead to rectification proceedings and administrative strike-off of the RCSL registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership taxable-results information return for the tax-transparent SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May following the tax year for a calendar-year taxpayer; extensions may be granted through the electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax, plus late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; failure to file may trigger ex-officio assessment; no direct RCSL strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal business tax annual return (déclaration de l'impôt commercial communal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for the communal authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the financial year-end; for calendar year-end, due by 31 May unless an extension is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Ex-officio assessment, late-payment interest at 0.6% per month, and administrative penalties up to EUR 1,000; persistent failure may also be treated as tax evasion and escalate to criminal sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent statutory audit if the SCSp exceeds at least two of three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total greater than EUR 4.4 million, net turnover greater than EUR 8.8 million, and average annual workforce greater than 50 employees; a consolidated group obligation may also apply where the SCSp is part of a controlled group.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on undertakings and accounting, as amended; IFRS as endorsed by the EU may be used where applicable for consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must identify, record, and annually confirm its ultimate beneficial owners in the RBE between 1 January and 31 March. Changes to ownership or control must be filed within one month. For an SCSp, any natural person directly or indirectly holding more than 25% of partnership interests or exercising control through other means must be disclosed; nominee arrangements must be stripped away for UBO identification.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of limited partners (ownership interests, contributions, distributions, and transfers)
Register of beneficial owners (internal RBE documentation and supporting KYC file)
General partner's minute book and decision records (required where the general partner is a corporate entity)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined 24.94% (Luxembourg City) = 17% CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax + 7% employment-fund surcharge on CIT; the SCSp itself is fiscally transparent, so the 17%/24.94% rate applies only to corporate partners on their allocable share or upon a check-the-box-like opaque election.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box: 80% exemption on qualifying IP-derived net income (effective combined rate ±4.94%); 20% R&D tax credit; notional interest deduction on new equity; participation exemption at partner level; no subscription-or-commerce-specific holiday.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Partnership information return under the Form 700 series ('Déclaration pour l'établissement de la base d'imposition') filed through MyGuichet.lu / ACD 'espace professionnel'; resident and non-resident corporate partners attach their own Form 700; resident individual partners attach personal income tax return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 May following the fiscal year-end; extended automatically to 31 December of the same year for electronic filings lodged by a registered tax adviser.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp name, RCS number, LEI, registered office, fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the Luxembourg address of the GP's registered office; do not list the non-resident partners as Luxembourg taxpayers unless a PE exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B – Legal form / tax status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the vehicle is an SCSp (no legal personality) and that no opaque taxation option has been exercised.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark 'fiscally transparent'; attach a copy of the partnership agreement if requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership profit/loss before distributions and the waterfall allocation per partner (% and amounts).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the non-resident partners' allocable share separately; only income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment of the partner is locally taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D – Municipal business tax base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial profit attributable to the Luxembourg business establishment (subscription-box fulfillment, local employees and decision-making).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident partner holds only a passive capital interest, state 'no commercial enterprise in Luxembourg' and document the absence of a fixed place of business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of intra-group transactions (platform fees, IP royalties, purchasing, logistics) with pricing and method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach local file if combined related-party flows exceed EUR 1,000,000; non-resident partners with no Luxembourg PE may cross-reference the group master file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section F – Withholding and refund statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that no dividend withholding is triggered by the SCSp's transparent status and any foreign WHT is reported.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners claim foreign tax credits in residence country; no Luxembourg ACD action required.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine up to EUR 25,000 (AO Art. 170); late-payment interest 0.6% per month (AO Art. 155); criminal tax-fraud fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment for willful concealment (AO Art. 426).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions from a transparent SCSp (no corporate taxpayer, no withholding). If the SCSp or its operator elects opaque corporate taxation, only then does the statutory 15% dividend WHT apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Since no WHT exists on transparent SCSp distributions, treaty relief is irrelevant at source. In the opaque-election scenario: deliver to the paying agent (i) tax residence certificate (issued within 6 months), (ii) standard Luxembourg relief-at-source form, and (iii) proof of beneficial ownership; the withholding agent applies the DTA rate immediately, and conclusions on audits are governed by the ACD — refund claims must be filed with the ACD if excess WHT was recovered.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic WHT on interest and royalties: 0% for arm's-length payments (including IP licensing connected to the subscription-box platform); DTA rates are therefore of no practical relevance, except for profit-participating loans or hybrid reverse-hybrid payments under ATAD.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 1,000,000 local-file trigger for related-party transactions when the MNE group has consolidated turnover of at least EUR 750,000,000; master file and CbCR similarly anchored to the EUR 750,000,000 group threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No dedicated ESR statute; Luxembourg enforces substance through the GAAR (AO Art. 6), the OECD principal-purpose test in tax treaties, the Bevola/Danish-case anti-shelter jurisprudence, and the ATAD. The subscription-box business must demonstrably exercise subscription management, fulfillment, procurement and risk control in Luxembourg to justify profit attribution to the local PE; otherwise profits are reallocated and treaty benefits are denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of subscription-box turnover from the partnership return, false allocation of revenue to a non-resident partner without local decision-making, or fake PE shifting to obtain a more favorable DTA position.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years (AO Art. 426); statutory reassessment extended to 10 years; late-payment interest at 0.6%/month; confiscation of illegal gains.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a corporate GP face joint civil liability for the tax debt of the partnership under the 'action en comblement du passif' where the debt results from an abusive fault; criminal courts may impose management bans, travel restrictions for serious fraud offenses and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Running the SCSp as a letterbox with no subscription-box activity in Luxembourg (no employees, no local procurement/fulfillment decisions, no local bank account or management), while deductions or platform benefits are claimed in Luxembourg or conduit royalties are passed through.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Requalification as opaque or reallocation of income (AO Art. 61); denial of treaty benefits under PPT; municipal business tax assessment plus 0.6%/month interest; penalties up to EUR 25,000; automatic AEOI look-through flagging (DAC6/hub-and-spoke arrangements).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil veil-piercing under the doctrine of abuse of law, personal restitution for dividends extracted without substance, and criminal liability where shell-company operations facilitate tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Stripe/Authorize.Net subscription proceeds under shell or nominee partner identities; failing to identify beneficial owners or to report suspicious e-commerce transactions; wiring profits to tax-haven partner accounts without KYC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004, as amended: administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for legal persons; criminal sanctions up to 5 years' imprisonment; freezing orders by the FIU; compelled deregistration and liquidation of the SCSp.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal fines and imprisonment for the GP's directors when they authorize or tolerate suspicious transactions; travel bans and director-disqualification orders issued by the Luxembourg criminal court.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Exceeding the EUR 1,000,000 related-party threshold without preparing the local file; pricing the subscription-box platform or IP royalties without a defensible CUP/TNMM benchmark; absence of written pricing policy; non-cooperation with the ACD's TP audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward TP adjustment with 0.6%/month interest; penalties up to EUR 250,000 for incomplete documentation (AO Arts. 166–171); potential double taxation if the corresponding adjustment is not obtained abroad; criminal exposure where false documentation is submitted.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign knowingly false TP documentation face criminal liability for tax fraud; civil liability for the uncollected corporate tax under the comblement du passif action.
